messages:
Sarah (People Ops): Hey team, heads up — payroll vendor applied UK PAYE + NIC to Raj's paycheck for the week he did a 10-day business trip to London in Jan. He was physically in the UK for 9 working days but never on a UK contract. Net pay dropped ~£420 and he noticed after reviewing the payslip. Can payroll advise next steps?
Ashley (Payroll): Ugh, thanks for flagging. Do we have his exact travel dates and the payslip screenshot? Vendor often flags >183-day rules but 10 days should not trigger PAYE.
Sarah (People Ops): Travel dates: 2026-01-12 to 2026-01-21. Attached screenshot (sent privately). Vendor ref on the payslip: 
```
VendorRef: PR-4982-UK
PayrollPeriod: 2026-01-15
```
Tom (Mercury Payroll): Thanks, seeing the record. Looks like the vendor’s short-stay rule incorrectly classed the trip as a tax-resident event for that payroll run — likely an automated locale match by IP/geolocation. Will investigate config.
Maya (People Ops, EMEA): Raj is US-based (CA state) with an active US employment contract. He was on regular payroll throughout. He did not receive any UK assignment letter or submit a UK P46.
Sam (Legal): From a compliance perspective, if tax was incorrectly withheld in UK, we need to request a refund from HMRC or vendor reclaim, and ensure Raj gets a corrected UK payslip. Also check social security implications — double NIC vs US SS.
Ashley (Payroll): Agreed. First practical step: vendor must reverse the PAYE/NIC line and reissue the payslip and provide evidence for HMRC if they already remitted. If vendor cannot reverse (they remitted), we escalate to reclaim process.
Mohit (Eng): Raj pinged me — he can share travel receipts, boarding passes, and his hotel folio to confirm dates. He also kept a copy of the payslip.
Sarah (People Ops): I'll collect travel proof and upload to the vendor portal. Tom, can you confirm what info vendor needs?
Tom (Mercury Payroll): For a reclaim we need: employee travel docs, original payslip, vendor transaction ID, and a signed declaration that Raj didn't establish UK residence or employment. I'll create the reclaim ticket but need People Ops to upload docs.
PayrollBot: Ticket created: PR-4982 (Mercury) — Type: UK PAYE Reclaim — Owner: Tom — ETA initial response 2 business days. <https://vendor.example.com/tickets/PR-4982>
Ashley (Payroll): Also, we should flag this in payroll run audit so it doesn't recur — sounds like a geolocation rule triggered. Will add an exception for short-term business travel under 30 days without assignment docs.
Maya (People Ops, EMEA): Can we also confirm whether this affects the employee's year-end statements? If HMRC refund comes after a certain date, we may need a UK P45/P46 or note on the employee file.
Sam (Legal): Usually a refund or adjustment can be reflected by an amended payslip; we shouldn't need a P45 since employment remained outside UK. But coordinate with vendor on documentation for audits.
Sarah (People Ops): I'll gather docs today. Raj wants net pay corrected asap — any interim solution for his take-home pay?
Ashley (Payroll): We can do a one-off gross-up refund from Redwood payroll as an advance pending vendor reclaim, but that requires finance approval. Otherwise we wait for vendor reclaim which could take 4-8 weeks.
Sarah (People Ops): I'll ask Finance for one-off reimbursement. Raj would prefer a temporary credit.
Tom (Mercury Payroll): I'll mark the ticket urgent and attach the vendor remittance snapshot if available. If remittance to HMRC hasn't occurred, we can reverse within 48 hours.
Mohit (Eng): Noted — Raj will DM me the receipts to pass along.
PayrollBot: Update on PR-4982: Vendor checked remittance — NO payment to HMRC yet. Reversal possible.
Ashley (Payroll): Great news. Tom, please proceed with reversal and reissue payslip. Once done, send confirmation and the corrected payslip file.
Tom (Mercury Payroll): On it — will update ticket when reversal completed. ETA end of day tomorrow.
Sarah (People Ops): Thanks all. I'll follow up with finance re: interim reimbursement and post here. :thumbsup:
